## Statute
§1(c)(v) - Tax rates for unmarried individuals
§63(c)(2)(C) - Standard deduction for unmarried individuals
§151(c) - Additional exemption for dependents
§151(d)(1) - Personal exemption amount
§151(d)(3)(B) - Phaseout applicable percentage
§68(b)(3)(C) - Applicable amount for unmarried individuals
§152(d) - Qualifying relative rules

## Reasoning
Alice is an unmarried individual (not married, not a surviving spouse, not head of household). Her gross income is $311,510.

Bob is Alice's father with no income in 2015. Under §152(d), Bob qualifies as Alice's dependent as a qualifying relative because:
- Relationship test (§152(d)(2)(C)): Father qualifies
- Income test (§152(d)(1)(B)): Bob has no income
- Not a qualifying child (§152(d)(1)(D)): Bob is an adult

Under §151(c), Alice can claim an additional exemption for Bob.

Under §63(c)(2)(C), Alice's standard deduction is $3,000.

Under §151(d)(1), the exemption amount is $2,000 per person. Alice claims 2 exemptions ($2,000 for herself + $2,000 for Bob = $4,000), subject to phaseout.

Under §68(b)(3)(C), the applicable amount for unmarried individuals is $250,000. Alice's AGI of $311,510 exceeds this by $61,510.

Under §151(d)(3)(B), the applicable percentage is 2 percentage points for each $2,500 (or fraction thereof) by which AGI exceeds the applicable amount.

Excess = $61,510. Number of $2,500 units = $61,510 / $2,500 = 24.604, which rounds up to 25 (fraction thereof).

Applicable percentage = 2% × 25 = 50%.

Total exemptions ($4,000) reduced by 50% = $2,000.

Taxable income = $311,510 - $3,000 - $2,000 = $306,510.

Under §1(c)(v), for taxable income over $250,000, tax = $79,772 + 39.6% of excess over $250,000.

Tax = $79,772 + 0.396 × ($306,510 - $250,000)
    = $79,772 + 0.396 × $56,510
    = $79,772 + $22,377.96
    = $102,149.96

Rounded to the nearest dollar: $102,150

Answer: 102150

        (A) $300,000 in the case of a joint return or a surviving spouse (as defined in section 2(a)),

        (B) $275,000 in the case of a head of household (as defined in section 2(b)),

        (C) $250,000 in the case of an individual who is not married and who is not a surviving spouse or head of household, and

        (D) 1/2 the amount applicable under subparagraph (A) in the case of a married individual filing a separate return.

    For purposes of this paragraph, marital status shall be determined under section 7703.

(f) Section not to apply

This section shall not apply to any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026.

§7703. Determination of marital status

(a) General rule

    (1) the determination of whether an individual is married shall be made as of the close of his taxable year; except that if his spouse dies during his taxable year such determination shall be made as of the time of such death; and

    (2) an individual legally separated from his spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance shall not be considered as married.

(b) Certain married individuals living apart

For purposes of those provisions of this title which refer to this subsection, if-

    (1) an individual who is married (within the meaning of subsection (a)) and who files a separate return maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of the taxable year the principal place of abode of a child with respect to whom such individual is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151,
